chapter: Japan trip, publishing and early influences
title: Bob Hope's low pay and the emptiness of great wealth
summary: Gil recalls Bob Hope underpaying his players and writers. The talk turns to rich people who cannot enjoy their money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: One can almost look at your face and tell you're not ( capable ?).
(LAUGHTER).

It's been proven over and over again that the human being is really not capable of having too much. You know, people degenerate when they're not really capable of having too much. They start much. The youngsters are messing things up. So there's really no reason why people should have too much. It's only show-offs, infantile showing off.

I worked for Bob Hope who would rather be listed as the ten men paying the highest income tax in the United States than pay a decent wage. He used to pay his players twenty five dollars a week. He used to pay his writers $150 a week whereas everybody else including Jack Benny who made his reputation as

being a skin flint when he isn't one, was paying his men about $1500 a week or something like that. So Bob Hope is one of the most, one of the cheapest most greedy men that's ever lived. You know he's got like $750,000,000.
That's right. That's what the figures........

He told me himself when I used to be close to him when I worked with him. He told me he arrived in Hollywood with $100,000 cash in the bank and nobody had ever heard of him. He had been playing in shows on Broadway before he ever became popular.
People get like that you know. They'd rather, it's just infantile show-off, you know, to have all that money. It really isn't necessary. That's what makes me sad about the whole scene.
And what does he do with this money that really puts joy and beauty into his life or anybody elses?
Does anybody with too much money really live? ( ? )
He's usually done a lot of wrong to get it. (LAUGHTER). Anybody in this country who can accumulate $750,000,000
Yes, and they can't use it sensibly after they get it really.
Because their joy simply comes out of making it.
Really. Just like the king in the counting house, counting all his money.
That's right, that's right.

I've asked two or three millionaires whom I've known rather well. For instance, when I taught at Penn State, oh Penn State is the state College of Pennsylvania, in a relatively small town, 30, 40 thousand people altogether. And they have a dozen millionaires, at least a dozen millionaires. And those that I knew almost never left the city, the town, let alone anything else. And so I said to one, one of them, I said you know, don't you ever learn want to go anywhere to see anything, anything about the rest of the world? He said, it doesn't interest me. He said, but I did go to Bermuda once and he said, you know, I really did enjoy that. I said, well you ought to try some of the other places you

might enjoy them too.
But in following through that conversation with him it was just the business of being able to make his ideas work and to get the money. And that was his job. And he actually worked in working clothes on his property.

And I said to him, now I'm the kind of person who hears of something going on in Paris over the weekend and I wanted to see it, if I had your kind of money I would be there. (LAUGHTER). But I'm like you. (LAUGHTER).

( ) went to Paris one time and he was there a couple of hours and he couldn't stay and he flew home. (LAUGHTER).
( ). Did you see the movie?
No I didn't see it.
It's like a cartoon movie, because in all the accidents and everything, nobody ever got hurt.
